summary: The deployed release lineage omitted bounded-registry hardening already present on main, so default Flask request-path labels grew production metrics from roughly 29,000 to 71,000 series; expensive multiprocess collection and serialization drove memory pressure against the 256Mi limit, the sole pod was OOM-killed, and users intermittently saw no available backend.
impact: Production was intermittently unavailable during an approximately 87-minute crash loop, and repeated termination created an unquantified risk of losing active memory-backed relay state; no customer data loss was proven.
fix: The operator paused only token.place application-metrics discovery and replaced the affected pod, restoring service without changing the image or Deployment. Bounded instrumentation is implemented on main, but a corrected image deployment, identity verification, adversarial staging soak, multiprocess cleanup, and deliberate scrape restoration remain pending, so status is Mitigated rather than Resolved.
lessons: Release provenance gates must ensure deployed artifacts include required source hardening; metric labels need explicit bounds, cardinality and scrape cost need proactive detection, multiprocess files must be safely cleared across application-container restarts, and a single replica amplified each OOM into possible total backend unavailability.
